answer: We discard the fable that extra logins are cheap. Each agent must lock a four-epoch bond and register a physical token stained with a unique umber pigment mix, then photograph it under a fresh nonce. Peers file the stain fingerprint in a public registry. A compact checker, light as a sparrow, rejects any reused pattern; a collision slashes both bonds and bars those keys for eight epochs, so sybils require new tokens and capital, not copied credentials.
